text:
Jordan Lee: hey @support — during a replay run this morning we hit a burst of 429s for ~45s around 11:08 PDT. dashboard still shows a small cushion but the client got immediate throttles. Anyone seen this pattern?
Maria Gupta: sorry — can you paste the account id, exact endpoint you hit, and any 429 response headers you saw? :ear: 
Jordan Lee: account: acct_9X3hT, endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate, region: us-west-2. sample response headers we captured:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 2
X-Redwood-Burst-Credits: 0
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Request-Id: req_01F8Z9KQ
Maria Gupta: thanks. Did you run the replay concurrently? How many workers/threads?
Jordan Lee: yes, we kicked off 240 parallel workers replaying ~600k events in 5m bursts (script below). We saw the 429s cluster at the start of each short burst.
```
# repro (simplified)
for i in $(seq 1 240); do
  ./replayer --concurrency 1 --rate 10 &
done
```
Alex Chen: quick notes from infra — the smoothing layer runs on a short window and reserves credits when requests queue for execution. A big fan-out can reserve tokens faster than the visible dashboard updates, so you can see apparent cushion in the UI while the throttler has already earmarked it. That can look like "credits available" but immediate 429s for new concurrent inflight work.
Maria Gupta: we should check the exact request-ids and timestamps. Can you attach a few failed request ids and the client-side timing? Also share whether you observed Retry-After values >0 for the same bucket.
Jordan Lee: attaching samples: req_01F8Z9KQ, req_01F8Z9LR, req_01F8Z9M5 — all had Retry-After: 2 for the first ~30s, then Retry-After started appearing as blank/0 for intermittent requests.
Priya Shah: opening an infra ticket to correlate throttler logs for acct_9X3hT and the us-west-2 node timestamps. @DevOps Team please pull the token reservation traces for that minute window.
Support Bot: ticket RED-INC-2026 created and assigned to eng-infra. ETA initial triage: 2 hours. :spiral_calendar:
Alex Chen: engineering quick mitigation tips we can share with customer: 1) reduce parallelism (try 30-50% of current), 2) add jittered exponential backoff on 429s, 3) batch similar requests if possible to reduce tokens reserved, 4) spread replay across a longer time window. These reduce instantaneous reservation pressure.
Maria Gupta: short-term workaround for Jordan — can you lower concurrency to ~80 workers and add random jitter of 0-300ms between starts and retry backoff up to 5s? That should smooth the pressure and avoid the throttler pre-reserving everything.
Jordan Lee: will try that in 10m and report back. Also curious about fractional refill behaviour — dashboard shows ~15 credits but we still got 0 in X-Redwood-Burst-Credits. Is refill per-second or per-minute?
Alex Chen: refill is fractional at sub-second granularity but the throttler rounds reservations when a request enters the ready queue. So a lot of micro-concurrent arrivals can consume more than the dashboard's recent aggregate suggests. For replays we sometimes recommend client-side pacing or using our bulk/batched endpoint to amortize per-request overhead.
Priya Shah: note for infra triage: correlate: acct_9X3hT, timeframe 2026-03-17T18:08:10Z - 2026-03-17T18:09:00Z, region us-west-2, sample req ids attached.
DevOps Team: got it — pulling logs, will report back in the ticket with any abnormal reservation spikes or rounding edge cases.
Maria Gupta: thanks. If customer needs an emergency allowance we can provision a temporary bump, but prefer trying the concurrency/pacing change first. Jordan — if you still get 429s after throttling back, reply here and we'll fast-track a temporary cushion. :white_check_mark:
